bug_semantics: PUT /api/echo/like/:id is registered on PublicRouterGroup (Gin /api group with no JWTAuthMiddleware). The handler and EchoService.LikeEcho perform an unbounded repository increment of echoes.fav_count for any known echo id, with no viewer/user binding, no per-principal dedup, and (before 4.7.3) no rate limit. An unauthenticated client that learns an echo UUID from the public timeline can repeat the PUT and linearly inflate fav_count, falsifying popularity/ranking and forcing cache invalidation on each write.
flaw_origin: The LikeEcho handler/service/repository (increment-only, no identity check) were first written earlier the same day in 290cf76168997a4d28897a892d3ec6f326d8eadc as unwired code. The smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerable attack surface is 5aa2fd32f9f87f0240a33f9aad0bb2db8dc725de, which added appRouterGroup.PublicRouterGroup.PUT("/echo/like/:id", h.EchoHandler.LikeEcho()) in internal/router/echo.go, exposing the unauthenticated mutating metric endpoint. Immediate parent 290cf76168997a4d28897a892d3ec6f326d8eadc has an empty Public section and no echo/like route.

reasoning: CVE-2026-79668 / GHSA-7v7f-8gw6-2q2x is a real, published CWE-306 integrity issue: unauthenticated unbounded increments of echo fav_count via PUT /api/echo/like/:id. CVE.org is PUBLISHED (not REJECTED/WITHDRAWN). Vendor GHSA-rgj7-vg8v-j4wr and GHSA-pj6q-4vq4-r8cg describe the same sink and name 4.7.3 as the patched bound. The complete reachable mechanism is the public route plus an increment that never binds a principal. git log -S and parent-tree inspection show 290cf761 first wrote LikeEcho (handler/service/repo, still no route). That is not the BIC: the advisory root cause is the explicitly public PUT, and without the route the increment is dead code. 5aa2fd32 is the smallest commit that first wrote PublicRouterGroup.PUT("/echo/like/:id", ...). Immediate parent 290cf761 lacks any echo/like registration (verified via git show of internal/router/echo.go and git grep). 5aa2fd32 is a single-parent feature commit, not a move/refactor/revert/squash. The public PUT then survives through v4.7.2 and is first constrained in cecc2c19 (ancestor of v4.7.3, not of v4.7.2) by per-IP rate limit plus (IP, echoID) hourly idempotency, which is the vendor's chosen remediation while keeping anonymous likes.
